gap: No result ChatGPT got turns the VA ratings into amps on the house circuit: APsystems EZ1-LV 900 VA = 7.5 A and Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV 360–500 VA = 3.0–4.17 A, so one EZ1 uses 75% of the 10 A dedicated circuit that rivals cite as its install condition, and the two-unit '1,800 W on a standard 15A circuit' setup on APsystems' own consumer page adds 15 A, the full rating of a 15 A circuit.
standout_why: Compared against solarwaypoint.com (cited), balconysolarkits.us (cited), pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited) and usa.apsystems.com EZ1 pages (cited). All give output only in VA or W. SolarWaypoint says outright that it gives no output current, efficiency or continuous-vs-peak figures. SolarWaypoint and PluginSolarCheck mention the EZ1's 10 A dedicated-circuit condition but do not give amps per inverter. None put APsystems' '1,800 W on a standard 15A circuit' claim next to that 10 A condition. None give Hoymiles' rated output current or its 95.5% CEC peak efficiency.
decides: This confirms the EZ1-LV as the two-panel pick, but only as a single unit: one unit at 7.5 A fits a 10 A dedicated circuit, while two units add 15 A. For a shopper who can't add a dedicated circuit, the HiFlow Pro LV adds only 3.0–4.17 A per unit. That makes it the low-load choice for one panel, which ChatGPT's 'budget' label doesn't explain.

findings.label: Max continuous AC output
findings.note: Product page says 'Max output power reaching 900VA'. It gives no W figure, no output current and no efficiency. The consumer page (usa.apsystems.com/ez1-consumers/) says 'Up to 900W AC output', so the maker uses both VA and W.

findings.label: Nominal AC output current
findings.source_title: APsystems EZ1 Microinverter – US Solar Supplier
findings.note: Retailer copy of the datasheet table. It matches the arithmetic 900 VA ÷ 120 V = 7.5 A. The maker's datasheet PDF could not be text-extracted. The page also lists max input current 18 A × 2, MPPT 27–45 V, peak efficiency 96%, and 'Maximum Units Supported: 2'.

findings.label: Maker's circuit claim for two units
findings.value: 1,800 W on a standard 15 A circuit (2 × 7.5 A = 15 A)
findings.note: Quote from a video description on the page (video dated 2026-10-12): 'Two EZ1 units can even be paired together for up to 1,800W of plug-in solar power on a standard 15A circuit.' Arithmetic: 1,800 W ÷ 120 V = 15 A, the full rating of a 15 A circuit. pv magazine USA (Ryan Kennedy, 2026-07-17) also reports 'Up to two EZ1-LV units can be connected in a single branch circuit.'

findings.label: Install condition as reported by a cited rival
findings.value: Dedicated 10 A circuit; 7.5 A is 75% of 10 A
findings.source_title: Which plug-in solar kits are UL 3700 certified? - PluginSolarCheck
findings.note: PluginSolarCheck lists 'a dedicated 10 A circuit' among the EZ1-LV installation conditions. SolarWaypoint says 'intended for dedicated circuits with a 10-amp breaker'. Neither page converts 900 VA to amps. This condition conflicts with APsystems' two-unit, 15 A circuit claim above.

findings.label: Rated output by model
findings.note: Maker page. One MPPT per unit. Max input current is 14 A (360/391/420), 15 A (450) or 16 A (500). Max input voltage is 64 V.

findings.label: CEC peak efficiency
findings.note: Labelled 'CEC peak efficiency', which is not CEC weighted efficiency. APsystems' only published figure is a 96% peak, which is not CEC-labelled, so the two can't be fairly compared.

findings.label: Rated AC output current
findings.source_title: Hoymiles HMS-360-1WM-LV HiFlow Pro LV 1-in-1 series plug-in microinverter - Northern Arizona Wind & Sun
findings.note: Retailer copy of the datasheet table. 360 VA ÷ 120 V = 3.0 A, which matches. By the same arithmetic the 500 VA model is 500 ÷ 120 = 4.17 A. The maker's datasheet PDF could not be text-extracted. Certifications listed: UL 1741, UL 3700, IEEE 1547.

findings.label: System cap (as stated by cited rivals)
findings.value: Up to 4 units / 1,200 W per system (1,200 W ÷ 120 V = 10 A)
findings.source_title: Which plug-in solar kits are UL 3700 certified? - PluginSolarCheck
findings.note: balconysolarkits.us/kits/ also gives 'up to 4 units and 1,200 W per home'. The amp conversion is my own arithmetic. I did not find this cap on the Hoymiles US page.
